newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubin repeats strong dlr in U.S. interests - FT.
newsitem.headline: Rubin repeats strong dlr in U.S. interests - FT.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin has repeated his stance that a strong dollar is in U.S. interests and that the dollar has been strong "for quite some time now", the Financial Times reported on Thursday.

"A strong dollar is in the country's interests. We've had a strong dollar for quite some time now," Rubin was quoted as saying in an interview with the newspaper. The Financial Times added that Rubin did not suggest that exchange rate management was the answer to the U.S. trade deficit, which it said he explained largely in terms of the high U.S. growth rate relative to the rest of the world and its low savings rate.
Rubin also said that the downside of the restructuring which has made U.S. business more competitive has been a growing hostility to further trade liberalisation, the Financial Times said.
"It's a much more difficult public environment for trade," the paper quoted him as saying. "Domestically, there is less support for liberalisation that there used to be and that's a big problem."

Rubin added he was concerned about the way the United States was turning inward. "It's very difficult to convey to the American people the importance to our national interest of the success of the rest of the world," he was quoted as saying.
Rubin said he expected solid growth and low U.S. inflation to continue, the paper said.

"My instinct is to think the most likely position going forward is pretty much what we've been having: solid growth and low inflation," the paper quoted him as saying two hours after the Federal Reserve on Tuesday raised short-term interest rates for the first time in more than two years.
Rubin said longer-term U.S. structural reforms in areas such as Medicare and social security would probably have to wait for the conclusion of a balanced budget deal.
"It will be difficult to get people to focus on those processes until balanced budget legislation is enacted," he was quoted as saying.
